chapter.name: Amendment of the Constitution
chapter.blurb: Article 368 procedure, the kinds of majority, the three ways of amendment and the landmark amendments from the 1st to the 106th.

scope_in.item: Simple, absolute, effective and special majorities

scope_out.item: Notes' listing of the President's election, courts and Article 368 as special majority only
scope_out.reason: contradicts the standard textbook and the notes' own later text; tested in the corrected form

scope_out.item: Years given for the 31st and 61st Amendments
scope_out.reason: notes and the standard textbook differ on the year; only the content is tested

concepts.name: Amendment procedure under Article 368 and the kinds of majority
concepts.description: Meaning of amendment, Article 368, the stage-by-stage procedure and the arithmetic of simple, absolute, effective and special majorities.
concepts.idea: An amendment Bill starts only in Parliament, needs a special majority in each House separately, no joint sitting, obligatory assent and, for federal provisions, ratification by half the States.
concepts.rule: Article 368 in Part XX gives Parliament the constituent power to amend, limited by the basic structure. A Bill may be introduced in either House by a Minister or a private member without the President's permission, must be passed by each House separately by a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting, with no joint sitting. Federal provisions also need ratification by half the State Legislatures by simple majority. The President must assent (24th Amendment, 1971). Simple majority is more than half of those present and voting; absolute majority is half of total membership (272 of 543); effective majority is of the strength less vacancies; Article 249 uses two-thirds present and voting; Article 61 uses two-thirds of the total membership (362).
concepts.example: With 480 of 543 members present, an Article 368 Bill needs 320 votes (higher than 272), while impeaching the President needs 362.

questions.q: The constituent power of Parliament to amend the Constitution, and the procedure for exercising it, are laid down in Article 368. In which Part of the Constitution is this Article placed?
o: Part XXI, Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions
questions.e: Article 368 sits in Part XX, which is devoted to the amendment of the Constitution.
w: Part XIX is the Miscellaneous part; it does not hold the amending power.
Part XVIII holds Articles 352-360 on emergencies.
Part XXI holds temporary and special provisions such as Articles 369-392.

questions.q: A Constitutional Amendment Bill has been passed by both Houses with the required majority and, where needed, ratified by the states. When it is presented to the President, which of the following correctly describes the constitutional position?
questions.a: The President must give assent and cannot withhold it or send it back for reconsideration, a position fixed by the 24th Amendment, 1971
o: The President must give assent and cannot withhold it or send it back for reconsideration, a position fixed by the 24th Amendment, 1971
The President may return it once for reconsideration, after which assent is compulsory, as laid down by the 24th Amendment, 1971
The President may withhold assent if the Bill touches a Fundamental Right, but must assent to any other amendment Bill
The President may refer the Bill to the Supreme Court for an opinion and may then withhold assent if the Court so advises
questions.e: The President must assent; there is no power to withhold or to return the Bill, and the 24th Amendment, 1971 made this obligatory. Assent is the formal act from which the Constitution stands amended.
w: Return for reconsideration is exactly what is denied for an amendment Bill; it is allowed only for ordinary Bills.
No category of amendment Bill lets the President withhold assent.
The President has no power to withhold assent after a reference to the Court for an amendment Bill.

questions.q: The Lok Sabha has 543 members, of whom 3 seats are vacant. When a Constitution (Amendment) Bill is put to vote, 500 members are present and voting. What is the minimum number of votes in favour needed for it to pass in the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: Two conditions apply: a majority of the total membership (543, vacancies ignored), i.e. 272, and two-thirds of the 500 present and voting, i.e. 334. The higher figure governs, so 334.
w: 362 is two-thirds of the whole House, the Article 61 impeachment requirement, not the Article 368 test.
272 satisfies only the first condition, the absolute majority.
271 is the effective majority of 540 and has no role in Article 368.

questions.q: In the 543-member Lok Sabha three seats are vacant. A resolution for the removal of the Speaker needs, at the minimum, the support of how many members?
questions.e: Removal of the Speaker needs an effective majority: more than half of the effective strength, which is 543 minus 3 vacancies = 540, so 271. The Vice-President's removal also uses the effective majority in the Rajya Sabha.
w: 272 is the absolute majority of the total strength of 543, not the effective majority.
270 is exactly half of 540, which is not a majority.
360 is two-thirds of 540 and is not required here.

questions.q: Under Article 61 a resolution for the impeachment of the President has to be passed in each House by a majority of
questions.a: not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House
o: not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House
not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting
a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting
a majority of the effective strength after deducting vacancies
questions.e: Article 61 asks for two-thirds of the total membership, a fixed number (362 in the 543-member Lok Sabha), not of the members present and voting.
w: Two-thirds of those present is the Article 249 majority.
This is the Article 368 formula for an amendment Bill.
The effective majority is used for the removal of the Vice-President or Speaker.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about amendment of the Constitution:

1. An amendment may add a new provision, modify an existing one or delete an obsolete one.
2. Amendments allow the Constitution to answer changing conditions while its foundational principles are preserved.
3. Article 368 places no limit on Parliament's constituent power, so even the basic structure may be amended.
4. A constitutional amendment is a formal change in the provisions of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The three forms of change are addition, variation and repeal. Statement 2 is correct: This is why it is called a dynamic, living document. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that the basic structure cannot be amended. Statement 4 is correct: That is the definition.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the initiation of a constitutional amendment:

1. It can be initiated only by introducing a Bill in either House of Parliament; a State Legislature cannot introduce an amendment Bill.
2. The Bill may be introduced by a Minister or by a private member.
3. Introduction needs the prior permission of the President.
4. Introduction is allowed only in the Rajya Sabha so that the States are represented.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. The Article 169 resolution on Legislative Councils is the one request a State may make. Statement 2 is correct: The Bill may be introduced by a Minister or by a private member. Statement 3 is incorrect: No prior permission is needed. Statement 4 is incorrect: It may be introduced in either House.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the role of the States in constitutional amendment:

1. An amendment affecting the federal structure also needs ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States.
2. The State Legislatures ratify such a Bill by a special majority of their own.
3. In the USA ratification by three-fourths of the States is required, so India is more flexible on this point.
4. The Constitution fixes a time limit within which the States must ratify.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: An amendment affecting the federal structure also needs ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States. Statement 2 is incorrect: Ratification is by a simple majority of the members present and voting. Statement 3 is correct: In the USA ratification by three-fourths of the States is required, so India is more flexible on this point. Statement 4 is incorrect: There is no time limit.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legislative stages of a Constitution Amendment Bill:

1. The joint-sitting provision of Article 108 does not apply to a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
2. The obligation of the President to assent was introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
3. After the President's assent the Bill becomes an Act and the Constitution stands amended.
4. Each House must pass the Bill separately, and a disagreement between the Houses cannot be resolved by a joint sitting.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: It came with the 24th Amendment Act, 1971. Statement 3 is correct: Assent is the formal act marking the date of amendment. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the kinds of majority:

1. A simple majority is a majority of the total membership of the House.
2. An absolute majority is a majority of the total membership of the House.
3. In the 543-member Lok Sabha the absolute majority is a fixed 272, whatever the attendance.
4. The effective majority is calculated on the total strength less the vacancies.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is a majority of the members present and voting. Statement 2 is correct: An absolute majority is a majority of the total membership of the House. Statement 3 is correct: Total membership is fixed, so 272 does not change with attendance. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the use of different majorities:

1. A simple majority is enough to pass an ordinary Bill, a Money Bill and a no-confidence motion.
2. An absolute majority is not prescribed on its own for any case; it figures only as one component of the special majority used for amending the Constitution.
3. The effective majority is used for the removal of the Vice-President and of the Speaker.
4. The impeachment of the President needs two-thirds of the members present and voting.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: simple majority covers ordinary, money and financial Bills and the no-confidence motion. Statement 2 is correct: an absolute majority is not prescribed on its own for any case and appears only as a component of the special majority used for amending the Constitution under Article 368. Statement 3 is correct: the effective majority is used for the removal of the Vice-President in the Rajya Sabha and of the Speaker; the Vice-President's removal resolution must also be agreed to by the Lok Sabha by simple majority. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 61 needs two-thirds of the total membership, not of those present and voting.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Article 249 is based on a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. If 480 members are present and voting, two-thirds of them is 320.
3. Article 249 enables Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest when such a majority supports it.
4. The Article 368 special majority is a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting, and the higher of the two requirements governs.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the resolution is passed in the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is correct: 480 x 2/3 = 320. Statement 3 is correct: on Centre-State relations. Statement 4 is correct: The Article 368 special majority is a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting, and the higher of the two requirements governs.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the majorities required for removal and approval:

1. The removal of a Judge of a High Court needs the same majority as the impeachment of the President under Article 61.
2. The Rajya Sabha elects its Deputy Chairman by an absolute majority.
3. The majority needed to remove a Judge of the Supreme Court is the one used for ordinary amendments under Article 368.
4. Parliamentary approval of the imposition of President's Rule needs the special majority of Article 368.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: a High Court Judge is removed by the Article 368-type majority (a majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of those present and voting), whereas Article 61 asks for two-thirds of the total membership. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Deputy Chairman is elected by simple majority; an absolute majority is never a standalone requirement. Statement 3 is correct: removal of a Supreme Court Judge falls under special majority-I, the same as Article 368. Statement 4 is incorrect: approval of President's Rule needs only a simple majority.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
A simple majority means more than half of the members present and voting. In the light of this, consider the following statements:

1. India has no separate constitutional convention or special body for amending the Constitution, unlike the USA.
2. Where 270 members are present and voting, 135 votes in favour are enough for a simple majority.
3. Where 480 members are present and voting, 240 votes in favour are enough for a simple majority.
4. Most amendments need only a majority of members present and voting in each House.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: India has no separate constitutional convention or special body for amending the Constitution, unlike the USA. Statement 2 is incorrect: 135 is exactly half of 270, which would be a tie; more than half needs at least 136. Statement 3 is incorrect: 240 is exactly half of 480; at least 241 votes are needed. Statement 4 is incorrect: most amendments need a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:
tr: Exactly half is not a majority

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A State Legislature cannot initiate an amendment Bill, but it may pass a resolution asking Parliament to create or abolish its Legislative Council.
2. The power to amend rests with Parliament, and the State Legislatures take part only in a few cases, through ratification.
3. A Constitution Amendment Bill can be introduced only by a Minister, not by a private member.
4. Parliament is bound to accept a State's resolution asking for creation or abolition of its Legislative Council.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct:(criticism 1 and 3). Statement 3 is incorrect: A private member can also introduce it. Statement 4 is incorrect: Parliament may approve, disapprove or take no action. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In India a special convention or body is convened for amending the Constitution, as in the USA.
2. In the USA the ratification by three-fourths of the States is needed, whereas India needs at least half.
3. Once the legislatures of half of the States ratify, inaction by the remaining States does not matter.
4. Amendments let the Constitution evolve while its foundational principles are preserved.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: India has no such body. Statement 2 is correct: In the USA the ratification by three-fourths of the States is needed, whereas India needs at least half. Statement 3 is correct: Once the legislatures of half of the States ratify, inaction by the remaining States does not matter. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the majorities required for particular decisions:

1. A resolution under Article 249 empowering Parliament to legislate on a State List subject is passed in the Rajya Sabha by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. Parliamentary approval of the proclamation of a National Emergency needs only a simple majority.
3. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed by an effective majority.
4. Parliamentary approval of a financial emergency under Article 360 needs a special majority of the Article 368 type.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 249 uses two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: approval of a National Emergency needs a majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of those present and voting. Statement 3 is incorrect: removal of the Chief Election Commissioner is by the special majority of the Article 368 type, not an effective majority. Statement 4 is incorrect: approval of a financial emergency needs only a simple majority. So exactly one statement is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: statement 1 is correct, so at least one statement is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: statements 2, 3 and 4 each misstate the majority, so only statement 1 is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: only statement 1 is correct; the other three misstate the majority needed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The President cannot withhold assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
Statement-II: A disagreement between the two Houses over a Constitutional Amendment Bill cannot be resolved by a joint sitting under Article 108.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the 24th Amendment made assent obligatory. Statement-II is correct: each House must pass the Bill separately and the joint-sitting provision does not apply. Statement-II concerns the passage of the Bill between the Houses, not the President's assent, so it does not explain Statement-I.
w: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I; they are separate facts.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: When 480 of the 543 Lok Sabha members are present and voting, a resolution to impeach the President needs more votes in the House than an Article 368 amendment Bill does.
Statement-II: Article 61 asks for two-thirds of the total membership, a fixed number, whereas the two-thirds limb of Article 368 is counted only on the members present and voting.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: 362 against 320. Statement-II is correct: and is the reason: the base of two-thirds is the whole House in Article 61 and only those present in Article 368.
w: Statement-II does give the reason for Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the kind of majority in List-I with the decision for which the Constitution requires it in List-II.

List-I
A. Simple majority
B. Effective majority
C. Majority of the total membership plus two-thirds of those present and voting
D. Two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha

List-II
1. Approval of the imposition of President's Rule
2. Removal of the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
3. Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court
4. Recommendation for creating a new All-India Service
questions.e: A: approval of President's Rule (Article 356) is by simple majority. B: removal of the Deputy Chairman (Article 90) needs an effective majority of all the then members. C: removal of a Supreme Court Judge needs the special majority of the Article 368 type. D: the Article 312 recommendation for a new All-India Service needs two-thirds of the Rajya Sabha members present and voting.
w: A and B are interchanged: President's Rule approval is a simple-majority matter and the Deputy Chairman's removal needs an effective majority.
B and C are interchanged: a Supreme Court Judge is removed by the Article 368-type special majority, the Deputy Chairman by an effective majority.
C and D are interchanged: the All-India Service resolution needs two-thirds of those present and voting in the Rajya Sabha, the judge's removal the Article 368-type majority.

concepts.name: Three ways of amendment and the early amendments, 1st to 42nd
concepts.description: Matters changed by simple majority, special majority and special majority with ratification, plus the amendments from the 1st to the 42nd.
concepts.idea: The Constitution is amended in three ways, and early amendments tie landmark changes to numbers (1st Ninth Schedule, 7th reorganisation, 42nd Mini-Constitution).
concepts.rule: Parliament may change by simple majority, outside Article 368, items such as new States (Articles 2-3), Legislative Councils (169), the Second Schedule, quorum, MPs' pay, citizenship, electoral laws, Union Territories and the Fifth and Sixth Schedules. Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and all other provisions need the special majority; federal provisions (President's election, courts, Seventh Schedule lists, representation of States, Article 368 itself) also need State ratification. Early amendments: 1st Ninth Schedule and Article 19 grounds, 4th Article 31A, 7th 14 States and 6 UTs, 9th Berubari, 11th Vice-President's electoral college, 24th, 25th, 26th privy purses, 31st 545 seats, 36th Sikkim, 38th, 39th, 42nd.
concepts.example: A State Assembly's resolution under Article 169 lets Parliament abolish a Council by an ordinary law, which is not an Article 368 amendment.

questions.q: Certain provisions of the Constitution can be changed by a simple majority of Parliament under articles other than Article 368. Which of the following describes the legal status of such changes?
questions.a: They fall outside Article 368 and are not counted as constitutional amendments under it
o: They fall outside Article 368 and are not counted as constitutional amendments under it
They are amendments under Article 368 that are exempt from the special-majority requirement
They are amendments under Article 368 that additionally need ratification by the legislatures of half of the States
They take effect as ordinary laws and therefore remain open to repeal or modification by any State Legislature
questions.e: Articles such as 2, 3 and 169 let Parliament alter the Constitution by simple majority; these are not deemed amendments under Article 368.
w: Such changes lie outside Article 368 altogether, so no exemption is being granted within it.
No State ratification is involved in these changes.
A State Legislature has no power to repeal a law of Parliament.

questions.q: The Legislative Assembly of a State passes, by the special majority prescribed in Article 169, a resolution for abolition of its Legislative Council. Which of the following is the correct position?
questions.a: Parliament may make the change by a law passed by simple majority, which is not an amendment under Article 368, and it is free to take no action
o: Parliament may make the change by a law passed by simple majority, which is not an amendment under Article 368, and it is free to take no action
Parliament must enact a constitutional amendment under Article 368 by special majority and obtain ratification from half of the States
Parliament is bound to give effect to the resolution by a law passed by simple majority within a reasonable time
Parliament may act only after the Legislative Council itself has passed a resolution supporting its own abolition by a two-thirds majority
questions.e: Creation or abolition of a Council is under Article 169 and is done by a simple-majority law outside Article 368; the State's request is the only initiative a State can take, and Parliament may approve, disapprove or ignore it.
w: The Article 368 route with ratification is not used for Article 169 changes.
Parliament is not bound by the State's resolution.
The Constitution requires no support resolution from the Council itself.

questions.q: A student argues that, since the Fundamental Rights are protected, they can never be touched by Parliament. Which of the following gives the correct constitutional position on amending Part III?
questions.a: Part III can be amended by a special majority under Article 368(2), without State ratification, subject to the basic structure limit set in Kesavananda Bharati
o: Part III can be amended by a special majority under Article 368(2), without State ratification, subject to the basic structure limit set in Kesavananda Bharati
Part III can be amended only with a special majority of Parliament plus ratification by half of the State Legislatures, as it limits State power
Part III can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament outside Article 368, as it concerns the rights of individuals
Part III cannot be amended at all by Parliament, since the Supreme Court has declared every right part of the basic structure
questions.e: Fundamental Rights fall in the special-majority category and attract no State ratification, but the basic structure doctrine limits Parliament.
w: Ratification is for federal provisions, not for Part III.
Simple majority outside Article 368 covers items such as citizenship and delimitation, not Part III.
The Court has not placed every right in the basic structure.

questions.q: The abolition of the classification of States into Parts A, B, C and D and their reorganisation into 14 States and 6 Union Territories was brought about by the
questions.e: The 7th Amendment (1956), following the States Reorganisation, replaced the Part A/B/C/D scheme with 14 States and 6 Union Territories.
w: The 1st Amendment added the Ninth Schedule and the new restrictions on Article 19.
The 4th Amendment widened Article 31A.
The 36th Amendment made Sikkim a State.

questions.q: Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Indian Union through the
questions.e: The 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a State; the preceding 35th had given it only the status of an associate State.
w: The 35th Amendment, 1974 made Sikkim only an associate State.
The 31st Amendment raised the Lok Sabha strength to 545.
The 38th Amendment made Emergency proclamations non-justiciable.

questions.q:
Consider the following matters that can be changed by a simple majority of Parliament:

1. Quorum in Parliament (Article 100) and the rules of procedure (Article 118).
2. Salaries and allowances of members of Parliament (Article 106).
3. The number of puisne judges of the Supreme Court (Article 124).
4. The Fifth Schedule on Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes and the Sixth Schedule on tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Quorum in Parliament (Article 100) and the rules of procedure (Article 118). Statement 2 is correct: Salaries and allowances of members of Parliament (Article 106). Statement 3 is correct: The number of puisne judges of the Supreme Court (Article 124). Statement 4 is correct: The Fifth Schedule on Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes and the Sixth Schedule on tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Which of the following statements regarding the amendment of the Constitution are correct?

1. Formation of new States and alteration of the areas, boundaries or names of existing States need a special majority under Article 368.
2. Acquisition and termination of citizenship (Articles 5-11) can be amended by a simple majority.
3. Electoral laws for Parliament and State Legislatures and delimitation of constituencies can be amended by a simple majority.
4. The provisions on governance of Union Territories (Articles 239-241) can be amended by a simple majority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: They fall under Articles 2 and 3 and need only a simple majority. Statement 2 is correct: Acquisition and termination of citizenship (Articles 5-11) can be amended by a simple majority. Statement 3 is correct: Electoral laws for Parliament and State Legislatures and delimitation of constituencies can be amended by a simple majority. Statement 4 is correct: The provisions on governance of Union Territories (Articles 239-241) can be amended by a simple majority.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the amendment of Parts III, IV and XVIII:

1. Under Article 368(2) each House must pass the Bill separately by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting.
2. The Directive Principles of State Policy are amended by the special majority.
3. The Emergency provisions in Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) can be amended by a simple majority.
4. Within the provisions on Parliament (Articles 79-122), matters such as quorum, rules of procedure and privileges are specially excluded and can be changed by a simple majority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 368(2) each House must pass the Bill separately by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting. Statement 2 is correct: The Directive Principles of State Policy are amended by the special majority. Statement 3 is incorrect: They need the special majority of Article 368. Statement 4 is correct: (the broad range there is only roughly right, so only the exclusions are tested).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the provisions that need ratification by half of the State Legislatures in addition to a special majority:

1. The election of the President and its manner (Articles 54 and 55) is such a provision.
2. The provisions concerning the Supreme Court and the High Courts are such provisions.
3. Article 368 itself, i.e. the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure, can be amended by a special majority alone, without State ratification.
4. Increasing the number of Supreme Court judges also needs the consent of half of the State Legislatures.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Articles 54 and 55 (election of the President and its manner) are listed in the proviso to Article 368(2), so they need ratification by half of the State Legislatures as well. Statement 2 is correct: the provisions on the Supreme Court and the High Courts are in the same proviso; the number of Supreme Court judges is the exception, since Parliament fixes it by ordinary law (simple majority). Statement 3 is incorrect: the proviso to Article 368(2) also covers Article 368 itself, so State ratification is needed there too. Statement 4 is incorrect: the number of Supreme Court judges is fixed by Parliament under Article 124 by simple majority, with no State ratification.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about early amendments:

1. The First Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review.
2. The First Amendment (1951) made the right to property a legal right under Article 300A instead of a Fundamental Right.
3. The Fourth Amendment (1955) widened Article 31A and placed compensation for property acquisition beyond court scrutiny.
4. The First Amendment added public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement to an offence as grounds for restricting Article 19.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The First Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review. Statement 2 is incorrect: the right to property was reduced to a legal right under Article 300A by the 44th Amendment (1978), not the First. Statement 3 is correct: The Fourth Amendment (1955) widened Article 31A and placed compensation for property acquisition beyond court scrutiny. Statement 4 is correct: The First Amendment added public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement to an offence as grounds for restricting Article 19.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about amendments between 1960 and 1971:

1. The Ninth Amendment (1960) transferred the Berubari Union from Pakistan to India.
2. The Eleventh Amendment (1961) made the Vice-President elected by an electoral college instead of a joint sitting of both Houses.
3. The Twenty-fourth Amendment (1971), responding to Golak Nath, affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part, including Fundamental Rights.
4. The Twenty-fifth Amendment (1971) abolished the privy purses of former rulers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It gave effect to the Indo-Pak agreement of 1958 for the transfer of Berubari to Pakistan. Statement 2 is correct: The Eleventh Amendment (1961) made the Vice-President elected by an electoral college instead of a joint sitting of both Houses. Statement 3 is correct: The Twenty-fourth Amendment (1971), responding to Golak Nath, affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part, including Fundamental Rights. Statement 4 is incorrect: The 26th Amendment abolished privy purses; the 25th curtailed property rights.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Thirty-first Amendment increased the strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 550.
2. The Twenty-fifth Amendment curtailed the right to property and gave laws under Article 39(b) and (c) immunity from challenge under Articles 14, 19 and 31.
3. The Thirty-eighth Amendment placed election disputes of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial review.
4. The Twenty-sixth Amendment abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely States.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The increase was from 525 to 545. Statement 2 is correct: the immunity is through Article 31C. Statement 3 is incorrect: That was the 39th; the 38th made the Emergency proclamation and ordinances non-justiciable. Statement 4 is correct: The Twenty-sixth Amendment abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely States.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

3. It extended the term of the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies to seven years.
4. It added Administrative Tribunals as Part XIV-A.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct: It added the Fundamental Duties as Part IV-A. Statement 3 is incorrect: The extension was to six years. Statement 4 is correct: It added Administrative Tribunals as Part XIV-A.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976:

1. It shifted Education, Forests, Weights and Measures, Protection of Wild Animals and Birds, and Administration of Justice from the Concurrent List to the State List.
2. It froze the seats in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies on the basis of the 1991 census.
3. It made the Directive Principles override certain Fundamental Rights and curtailed judicial review.
4. In Minerva Mills (1980) the Supreme Court upheld the provisions giving the Directive Principles priority over Fundamental Rights.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The shift was the other way, from the State List to the Concurrent List. Statement 2 is incorrect: The freeze was on the basis of the 1971 census. Statement 3 is correct: It made the Directive Principles override certain Fundamental Rights and curtailed judicial review. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Court struck down those parts.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The use of English in Parliament and the official language provisions can be amended by a simple majority.
2. The Sixth Schedule on tribal areas needs a special majority, while the Fifth Schedule needs a simple majority.
3. The Second Schedule on emoluments and privileges of the President, Governors, Speakers and Judges can be amended by a simple majority.
4. The provisions on acquisition and termination of citizenship (Articles 5-11) need the special majority of Article 368.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The use of English in Parliament and the official language provisions can be amended by a simple majority. Statement 2 is incorrect: Both Schedules are amendable by simple majority. Statement 3 is correct: The Second Schedule on emoluments and privileges of the President, Governors, Speakers and Judges can be amended by a simple majority. Statement 4 is incorrect: citizenship provisions are amendable by simple majority outside Article 368. So exactly two statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' undercounts: statements 1 and 3 are both correct.
'Only three' overcounts: statements 2 and 4 are incorrect.
'None' undercounts: statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The First Amendment added the Ninth Schedule.
2. The Thirty-first Amendment raised the strength of the Lok Sabha to 545.
3. The Twenty-fourth Amendment reduced Parliament's power over Fundamental Rights.
4. The Fourth Amendment widened Article 31A in respect of compensation for acquisition of property.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The First Amendment added the Ninth Schedule. Statement 2 is correct: the Lok Sabha was enlarged from 525 to 545. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 24th Amendment affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part, including Fundamental Rights. Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly three statements are correct.
w: 'All four' overcounts: statement 3 is incorrect.
'Only two' undercounts: statements 1, 2 and 4 are all correct.
'Only one' undercounts: three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 39th Amendment placed election disputes of the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond the reach of the courts.
2. Administrative Tribunals in Part XIV-A were added by the 44th Amendment.
3. The 42nd Amendment extended the term of the Lok Sabha to six years but left the term of the State Assemblies at five.
4. The Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Amendment occupy ten Articles of Part IV-A.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the 39th Amendment of 1975 shielded such election disputes from judicial review. Statement 2 is incorrect: Administrative Tribunals were added by the 42nd Amendment. Statement 3 is incorrect: it extended the terms of both bodies. Statement 4 is incorrect: Part IV-A has a single Article, 51A. So exactly one statement is correct.
w: 'None' undercounts: statement 1 is correct.
'Only two' overcounts: statements 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect.
'Only three' overcounts: only statement 1 is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A law of Parliament creating a Legislative Council in a State is passed by simple majority, without the special majority and procedure of Article 368.
Statement-II: Article 169 itself provides that such a law is not to be deemed an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: a law creating (or abolishing) a Legislative Council is passed like an ordinary law by simple majority, after the State Assembly's special-majority resolution. Statement-II is correct: Article 169 says the law is not to be deemed an amendment for the purposes of Article 368, and that is exactly why the Article 368 procedure is not needed; Statement-II is the reason for Statement-I.
w: Statement-II does give the reason for Statement-I: the law is not an Article 368 amendment, so no special majority is needed.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The 38th Amendment (1975) made the declaration of Emergency and ordinances non-justiciable.
Statement-II: The 44th Amendment left these provisions of the 38th Amendment untouched.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The 38th Amendment (1975) made the declaration of Emergency and ordinances non-justiciable. Statement-II is incorrect: the 44th Amendment deleted the 38th Amendment's bar on judicial review of the Emergency proclamation.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so 'both correct' fails.
Statement-II is incorrect, so 'both correct' fails.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the Constitution Amendment Acts in List-I with their main effect in List-II.

List-I
A. Seventh Amendment
B. Eleventh Amendment
C. Thirty-sixth Amendment
D. Forty-second Amendment

List-II
1. Sikkim made a State of the Union
2. Vice-President elected by an electoral college
3. Words Socialist, Secular and Integrity added to the Preamble
4. Abolition of Part A/B/C/D classification of States
questions.e: 7th: Part A/B/C/D classification abolished; 11th: Vice-President elected by an electoral college; 36th: Sikkim made a State; 42nd: Preamble words added.
w: A and B are interchanged: the Part A-D classification went with the reorganisation of States, the electoral college with the 11th.
B and C are interchanged: the electoral college is the 11th and Sikkim the 36th.
Three pairs are misplaced: the 42nd is about the Preamble words, the 36th about Sikkim and the 7th about the States classification.

concepts.name: Amendments from the 44th to the 106th and the summary of majorities
concepts.description: Landmark amendments from 1978 to 2023 and the summary of the three types of amendment.
concepts.idea: From the 44th restoring safeguards to the 106th women's reservation, each amendment is tied to a number, a year and a change.
concepts.rule: The 44th (1978) restored the five-year term, made property a legal right (Article 300A), made Articles 20-21 non-suspendable, replaced internal disturbance by armed rebellion and required written Cabinet advice. The 52nd added the Tenth Schedule; 61st lowered the voting age to 18; 69th created Delhi NCT; 73rd and 74th (1992) added Parts IX and IXA; 86th inserted Article 21A; 91st capped ministers at 15% and deleted the split exemption; 92nd made 22 languages; 97th co-operatives; 99th NJAC (struck down 2015); 101st GST; 102nd NCBC; 103rd EWS 10%; 104th SC/ST seats to 2030 and end of Anglo-Indian nomination; 105th States' SEBC lists; 106th 33% women's reservation.
concepts.example: The 74th Amendment added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects, while the 73rd added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule with 29.

questions.q: Before the 44th Amendment, a National Emergency could be proclaimed on the President's own assessment. Which of the following was brought in by the 44th Amendment Act in relation to the proclamation of a National Emergency?
questions.a: The President can proclaim it only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet
o: The President can proclaim it only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet
The ground of armed rebellion was replaced by internal disturbance
The Emergency was made non-justiciable by barring review of the proclamation
Articles 19, 20 and 21 were made incapable of suspension during an Emergency
questions.e: The 44th Amendment required written Cabinet advice for the proclamation, replaced 'internal disturbance' by 'armed rebellion', and made Articles 20 and 21 non-suspendable.
w: It is the reverse: internal disturbance was the older ground and was replaced by armed rebellion.
Non-justiciability of the proclamation was the 38th Amendment's change, later reversed by the 44th.
Only Articles 20 and 21 were protected, not Article 19.

questions.q: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003, which capped the Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the strength of the House, also made which change to the anti-defection law introduced in 1985?
questions.a: It deleted the exemption for a split in a party and barred defectors from holding ministerial posts
o: It deleted the exemption for a split in a party and barred defectors from holding ministerial posts
It added the Tenth Schedule and gave the Speaker the power to decide disqualification
It raised the strength needed for a valid merger from two-thirds to three-fourths of the legislators of the party
It extended the disqualification to nominated members who joined a party after six months
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment (1985) introduced the Tenth Schedule; the 91st (2003) deleted the split exemption and barred defectors from ministerial posts.
w: The Tenth Schedule was the 52nd Amendment's contribution, not the 91st's.
The merger threshold was not changed; the 91st removed the split exemption and added the ministerial bar.
Treatment of nominated members is not the 91st Amendment's change.

questions.q: The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies. Which of the following correctly describes what it added to the Constitution?
questions.a: Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects
o: Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects
Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects
Part IXA and the Eleventh Schedule with 18 subjects
Part IXB and the Twelfth Schedule with 29 subjects
questions.e: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects); the 73rd inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).
w: That pairing belongs to the 73rd Amendment on Panchayats.
The Eleventh Schedule belongs to the Panchayats and has 29 subjects.
Part IXB is the 97th Amendment's addition on co-operative societies.

questions.q: After the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, Article 45 of the Directive Principles provides for
questions.a: a State duty to provide pre-school care and education to children until they complete six years of age
o: a State duty to provide pre-school care and education to children until they complete six years of age
free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years
free and compulsory education for children in the age group of six to fourteen years as a justiciable right
vocational training for children between six and fourteen years of age
questions.e: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A (elementary education, ages 6-14), added a Fundamental Duty (51A(k)) for parents and recast Article 45 for early childhood care below six.
w: That was the original wording of Article 45, which was recast.
The 6-14 right now sits in Article 21A, a Fundamental Right.
Vocational training is not what Article 45 says.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 in relation to the 42nd Amendment?
questions.a: It reversed several distortions of the 42nd Amendment and restored post-Emergency safeguards such as the five-year term of the Lok Sabha
o: It reversed several distortions of the 42nd Amendment and restored post-Emergency safeguards such as the five-year term of the Lok Sabha
It confirmed the 42nd Amendment and added a further extension of the term of the Lok Sabha to six years
It repealed the 42nd Amendment in full and restored the Constitution as it stood in 1950
It added Fundamental Duties to the Constitution as a response to the Swaran Singh Committee
questions.e: The 44th Amendment restored the five-year term and undid several 42nd changes; it did not repeal that Amendment wholesale.
w: The six-year term was a 42nd change that the 44th removed.
The 44th removed certain changes only; the Preamble words and Fundamental Duties remain.
Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment itself.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 44th Amendment Act, 1978:

1. It restored the five-year term of the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies.
2. It deleted the right to property as a Fundamental Right and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
3. It replaced internal disturbance with armed rebellion as a ground for National Emergency.
4. It made Articles 19, 20 and 21 non-suspendable during a National Emergency.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It restored the five-year term of the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies. Statement 2 is correct: It deleted the right to property as a Fundamental Right and made it a legal right under Article 300A. Statement 3 is correct: It replaced internal disturbance with armed rebellion as a ground for National Emergency. Statement 4 is incorrect: Only Articles 20 and 21 were made non-suspendable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about amendments of the 1980s and 1990s:

questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The 52nd added the Tenth Schedule on anti-defection; the Ninth Schedule came with the 1st Amendment. Statement 2 is correct: The 58th Amendment (1987) provided an authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution under Article 394A. Statement 3 is correct: Article 326. Statement 4 is correct: The 69th Amendment (1991) made Delhi the National Capital Territory with a 70-member Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers.

Consider the following statements:

1. The 65th Amendment (1990) set up a multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs in place of the Special Officer.
2. The 69th Amendment made Delhi a full-fledged State with a 70-member Assembly.
3. The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects.
4. The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: it was later split into two Commissions by the 89th Amendment. Statement 2 is incorrect: Delhi became a National Capital Territory, not a State. Statement 3 is correct: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects. Statement 4 is correct: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 71st Amendment (1992) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule, making 22 languages.
2. The 76th Amendment (1994) placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule, above the 50 per cent ceiling of Indra Sawhney.
3. The 77th Amendment (1995) provided reservation in promotions for the SCs and STs, nullifying a contrary Supreme Court ruling.
4. The 77th Amendment (1995) provided reservation in promotions for the Other Backward Classes.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, making 18; the four others came with the 92nd (2003). Statement 2 is correct: The 76th Amendment (1994) placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule, above the 50 per cent ceiling of Indra Sawhney. w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 86th Amendment (2002) made elementary education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
2. The 86th Amendment added the duty of parents and guardians as Article 51A(j).
3. The 91st Amendment (2003) capped the Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the strength of the House.
4. The 91st Amendment retained the split exemption from disqualification under the anti-defection law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The 86th Amendment (2002) made elementary education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right under Article 21A. Statement 2 is incorrect: It is clause (k) of Article 51A. Statement 3 is correct: The 91st Amendment (2003) capped the Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the strength of the House. Statement 4 is incorrect: It deleted the split exemption.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule, making 21 languages.
2. As inserted by the 97th Amendment (2011), Article 19 covers the right to form co-operative societies and the Constitution contains a Part IXB on co-operatives.
3. The 99th Amendment (2014) gave constitutional status to the Collegium system.
4. The Supreme Court upheld the NJAC amendment in 2015.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The four languages brought the number to 22, not 21. Statement 2 is correct: in Union of India v Rajendra N. Shah (2021) the Supreme Court held Part IXB invalid as far as State co-operative societies go, but the 97th Amendment did insert it and amend Article 19. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 99th created the NJAC to replace the Collegium. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Court struck it down in 2015 and the Collegium survived.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 100th Amendment (2015) gave effect to the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, affecting Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.
2. The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced GST, gave concurrent GST-legislating power to Parliament and the States and set up the GST Council.
3. The 102nd Amendment (2018) gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes.
4. The 103rd Amendment (2019) enabled up to 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in education and public employment over and above existing reservations.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The 100th Amendment (2015) gave effect to the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, affecting Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura. Statement 2 is correct: the 101st Amendment inserted Article 246A (concurrent power of Parliament and the States to legislate on GST) and Article 279A (the GST Council). Statement 3 is correct: The 102nd Amendment (2018) gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes. Statement 4 is correct: The 103rd Amendment (2019) enabled up to 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in education and public employment over and above existing reservations.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about recent amendments:

1. The 104th Amendment extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies until 2030.
2. The 104th Amendment extended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members for another ten years.
3. The 102nd Amendment gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
4. The 106th Amendment mandates 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The 104th Amendment extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies until 2030. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 104th discontinued Anglo-Indian nomination. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 102nd gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes; the SC commission had been constitutionalised earlier (65th Amendment). Statement 4 is correct: The 106th Amendment mandates 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly.

Consider the following statements:

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Act is numbered of 2019 but commenced in January 2020. Statement 2 is incorrect: it restored that power. Statement 3 is correct: The 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023 as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. Statement 4 is correct: Janhit Abhiyan (2022), decided 3:2.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the three ways of amending the Constitution:

1. Formation of new States is a simple-majority matter that falls outside Article 368.
2. Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles are amended by the special majority.
3. Special majority plus ratification by at least half the State Legislatures applies to what affects the federal structure and Centre-State relations.
4. The election of the President needs only the special majority, without ratification.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Formation of new States is a simple-majority matter that falls outside Article 368. Statement 2 is correct: Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles are amended by the special majority. Statement 3 is correct: Special majority plus ratification by at least half the State Legislatures applies to what affects the federal structure and Centre-State relations. Statement 4 is incorrect: It needs ratification by half the States. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 106th Amendment extends the one-third reservation for women to the Delhi Legislative Assembly as well.
2. The 105th Amendment restored the power of States to identify SEBC lists.
3. The women's reservation under the 106th Amendment took effect at once for the next general election.
4. The NJAC established by the 99th Amendment continues to operate.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the women's reservation covers the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly. Statement 2 is correct: The 105th Amendment restored the power of States to identify SEBC lists. Statement 3 is incorrect: it takes effect only after the first delimitation following the next census. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Supreme Court struck down the NJAC in 2015. So exactly two statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' undercounts: statements 1 and 2 are both correct.
'Only three' overcounts: statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.
'All four' overcounts: statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 100th Amendment gave effect to the land boundary agreement with Pakistan.
2. The 71st Amendment raised the number of languages in the Eighth Schedule to 22.
3. The 44th Amendment retained the right to property as a Fundamental Right under Article 31.
4. The 76th Amendment placed Karnataka's reservation law above the 50 per cent ceiling in the Ninth Schedule.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the 100th Amendment implemented the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 71st brought the number to 18; 22 came with the 92nd. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 44th deleted the right to property from Part III and made it a legal right under Article 300A. Statement 4 is incorrect: it was Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent law that was placed in the Ninth Schedule. So none of the statements is correct.
w: 'Only one' overcounts: every statement misstates its Amendment.
'Only two' overcounts: every statement misstates its Amendment.
'Only three' overcounts: every statement misstates its Amendment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Anglo-Indian nomination to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies ended with the 104th Amendment.
Statement-II: The 104th Amendment extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in these bodies until 2030.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct. The extension of SC/ST reservation is a separate provision of the same Amendment and does not explain why nomination ended.
w: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I; they are separate facts.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The 105th Amendment restored the power of States and Union Territories to identify their own SEBC lists.
Statement-II: After the 102nd Amendment the Supreme Court, in the Maratha reservation case, read the Commission's constitutional status as leaving the identification of SEBCs to the Centre.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The 105th Amendment restored the power of States and Union Territories to identify their own SEBC lists. Statement-II is correct: it describes the Maratha reservation ruling (Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil), after which the 105th Amendment was passed, so it is the reason for the restoration.
w: Statement-II does give the reason for Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the Constitution Amendment Acts in List-I with the subject each dealt with in List-II.

List-I
A. 61st Amendment
B. 65th Amendment
C. 101st Amendment
D. 58th Amendment

List-II
1. Age for registration as a voter brought down to 18 years
2. A multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs in place of a Special Officer
3. GST Council
4. Authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution
questions.e: 61st: voting age brought down to 18; 65th: multi-member Commission for SCs and STs; 101st: GST and the GST Council; 58th: authoritative Hindi text.
w: A and B are interchanged: the voting age belongs to the 61st and the Commission to the 65th.
C and D are interchanged: the GST Council is the 101st and the Hindi text the 58th.
A and D are interchanged: the voting age is the 61st and the Hindi text the 58th.
